name: Planck.js / web page
description: A standalone web page: an index.html that runs this scene in Planck.js on a canvas.

settings.label: Project name
settings.tooltip: The page title and the folder name inside package.json. Letters, digits and underscores.

settings.label: Add controls
settings.tooltip: Start, Pause and Stop buttons above the canvas. Without them the page opens running and there is nothing to press.

settings.label: Debug view
settings.tooltip: Adds a Debug view switch to the controls: joints, each body's centre of mass and heading, and where the rays are looking, drawn over the scene.

settings.label: Steps per second
settings.tooltip: How often the exported page steps the world. The editor's own setting is not carried across, since it is a preference rather than part of the scene.

settings.label: Where Planck.js comes from
settings.tooltip: cdn: index.html loads the library straight from the URL below, so the exported folder carries no copy of it and needs a network to open. npm: a package.json is written and the page expects node_modules, so 'npm install' fetches the repository and ref below.

settings.label: Planck.js URL
settings.tooltip: What index.html points its script tag at. {version} is replaced by the version below. Point it at a fork, a mirror, a company proxy or a copy you keep beside the page; whatever answers has to be a Planck.js v1 UMD build, which is what the generated code is written against.

settings.label: Planck.js version
settings.tooltip: Which release the URL above asks for, and what package.json depends on. The generated code is written against the v1 API.

settings.label: Planck.js repository
settings.tooltip: Used by the npm choice: package.json depends on this repository rather than on the registry. Point it at a fork or a mirror.

settings.label: Planck.js tag or branch
settings.tooltip: Which commit of that repository npm should take. Pinned to a tag by default, so the page builds the same way twice.
